text:
Ryan Leonard is having the kind of second season the Capitals drafted him eighth overall for. The 21-year-old from Northampton, Massachusetts, took a five-game point streak and a four-game goal streak into Washington's loss in Boston, and he has 9 goals and 17 points in 21 games despite playing only about 14 minutes a night.

Seven of those points came on the power play, and he leads plenty of top-six forwards with 56 shots on goal; his hardest shots sit in the 96th percentile of the league. He also plays with an edge (35 hits, and a fine for high-sticking the Devils' Cody Glass, per Sportsnet).

Some regression is coming on the goals: 9 on 6.4 expected, shooting 16% against a likely 11 to 16%. The defensive side is the thing to watch. Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting noticeably more chances with him on the ice last season (bottom 9% of forwards), and Washington is a bit worse at 5v5 with him on this year too. Among forwards picked sixth to tenth since 2005, the median first full season was 0.40 points a game. He's at 0.81.
